title: Spring MVC: REST, validation and errors
description: Spring MVC controllers and routing, status codes, Bean Validation, DTOs versus entities, and global error handling with @RestControllerAdvice and ProblemDetail.
source: Spring MVC and Bean Validation documentation; Spring Framework error responses (ProblemDetail, RFC 9457 which obsoletes RFC 7807); Spring Boot Jackson defaults; Baeldung
seriesDescription: Spring Boot structure and DI, REST and validation, error handling, filters, async, API design, jobs and health. JEE-Advanced style: integer, assertion-reason, matrix match, fill-in-the-blanks, short code and multi-correct questions.

questions.prompt: A Spring MVC controller takes @Valid @RequestBody CreateUserRequest. The JSON body violates a @NotBlank constraint and nothing else customises error handling. What HTTP status code does the client receive?
questions.explanation: The resolver throws MethodArgumentNotValidException, which DefaultHandlerExceptionResolver turns into 400 Bad Request.

questions.prompt: A request record is declared as CreateUser(@NotBlank String name, @Min(18) int age, @Email String email), and the controller parameter is annotated @Valid @RequestBody. A client posts {"name": "", "age": 10, "email": "not-an-email"}. How many constraint violations does the MethodArgumentNotValidException carry?
questions.explanation: Bean Validation checks every constraint and collects all violations instead of stopping at the first: blank name, age below 18 and a malformed e-mail give three. Returning all of them lets the client fix the form in one round trip.

questions.prompt: Write a Spring @RestController method for POST /users. It takes a validated CreateUserRequest body, calls service.create(req) which returns a UserResponse, and answers 201 Created with that body.
questions.explanation: ResponseEntity.created(uri).body(out) is even better because it sets the Location header. @ResponseStatus(HttpStatus.CREATED) on the method is another valid way.

questions.prompt: A controller declares @GetMapping("/users/{id}") first and @GetMapping("/users/me") second. What does GET /users/me invoke?

options.text: The /users/{id} handler with id = "me", and a 400 follows when it is converted to a number.
options.why: Pattern ranking happens before argument conversion, so the template never wins here.

options.text: Neither of them, because Spring detects the two overlapping templates at startup and fails with an ambiguous mapping error.
options.why: A literal path and a template are not ambiguous: the literal is simply more specific.

options.text: A 404, because two handlers match and Spring refuses to choose between them.
options.why: Spring always picks the best match when patterns differ in specificity.

options.text: The /users/me handler, because the more specific pattern ranks higher regardless of declaration order.
options.why: Correct: Spring MVC sorts matching patterns by specificity, so the literal path beats the template.

questions.explanation: Ambiguity errors appear only when two mappings are equally specific, for example the same path with the same method and conditions.

questions.prompt: Write a Spring global handler: a class annotated for all controllers with an @ExceptionHandler method for MethodArgumentNotValidException that returns a ProblemDetail with status 400 and the detail "Validation failed".
questions.explanation: ProblemDetail is Spring 6 / Boot 3's model of the RFC 9457 problem body (RFC 7807 before it was obsoleted), served as application/problem+json. Extending ResponseEntityExceptionHandler or setting spring.mvc.problemdetails.enabled=true are other common routes.

questions.prompt: Judge the assertion and the reason.
questions.assertion: In Bean Validation, a String field annotated only with @NotNull accepts the empty string.
questions.reason: @NotNull checks only that the value is not null.

whys.a: Correct: "" is not null, so @NotNull passes; @NotEmpty or @NotBlank is needed to reject it.
whys.b: Wrong: R is exactly the reason.

questions.explanation: NotNull < NotEmpty < NotBlank. NotBlank also rejects whitespace-only strings and applies to CharSequence only. Also remember @Size(min=3) passes null.

questions.prompt: Judge the assertion and the reason.
questions.assertion: In Spring, a @Valid failure on a @RequestBody makes Spring throw ConstraintViolationException.
questions.reason: A @Valid failure on a @RequestBody makes Spring throw MethodArgumentNotValidException.

whys.d: Correct: body binding errors raise MethodArgumentNotValidException; ConstraintViolationException belongs to method-level validation (@Validated).

questions.explanation: Handle MethodArgumentNotValidException for bodies and ConstraintViolationException (or HandlerMethodValidationException in Spring 6.1+) for parameters.

questions.prompt: Fill in the Spring MVC binding annotations.
questions.text: Use {1} to bind a segment of the URL path, {2} to bind a query-string parameter, and {3} to deserialise the JSON request body.
questions.explanation: @RequestHeader reads headers and @ModelAttribute binds form fields.

questions.prompt: Match each Bean Validation or Spring construct with its effect.

right.text: Rejects only null; an empty string passes
Rejects null and empty strings or collections
Rejects null, empty and whitespace-only text
Cascades validation into that nested object
Enables validation of method parameters such as @RequestParam
Rejects values that do not match a regular expression
Makes the field read-only after binding

questions.explanation: The last two entries explain why query and path parameters raise ConstraintViolationException (or HandlerMethodValidationException in newer versions) while bodies raise MethodArgumentNotValidException.

questions.prompt: Select all that apply: which statements about @RestControllerAdvice and @ExceptionHandler are correct?

options.text: The most specific matching exception type wins when several handlers could apply.
options.why: Spring picks the handler whose exception type is closest to the thrown one.

options.text: It also catches exceptions thrown inside Servlet filters.
options.why: Filters run before DispatcherServlet, so the advice never sees their exceptions.

options.text: basePackages or annotations can narrow an advice class to some controllers.
options.why: The selector attributes limit which controllers the advice covers.

options.text: Every handler method must return a ResponseEntity.
options.why: A body object, a ProblemDetail or void with @ResponseStatus are all accepted.

options.text: An exception class annotated with @ResponseStatus is turned into that status without a handler.
It applies only to the controller class in which it is declared.
options.why: A global advice applies to all controllers unless you narrow it.

questions.explanation: For errors thrown in filters, handle them in the filter itself or with an error controller. ProblemDetail gives a standard application/problem+json body.

questions.prompt: A client posts {"name": "Ann", "role": "admin"} to an endpoint whose request record declares only name. With stock Spring Boot settings, what happens to the unknown role field?

options.text: The request is rejected with 400 because role is not declared.
options.why: Plain Jackson would fail, but Boot turns that behaviour off by default.

options.text: It is silently ignored and the request succeeds.
options.why: Correct: Boot disables FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES on its auto-configured ObjectMapper.

options.text: The field is stored in a map on the record and kept for later.
options.why: A record has no place to keep undeclared fields.

options.text: Spring answers 422 Unprocessable Entity listing the extra field.
options.why: Spring MVC does not use 422 for binding problems on its own.

questions.explanation: Strictness is opt-in: spring.jackson.deserialization.fail-on-unknown-properties=true, or @JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown = false) on a class. Ignoring extras is also why binding request JSON straight into an entity invites mass assignment.

questions.prompt: Write the Java record CreateUserRequest with a non-blank String name, a String email that must be a well-formed address, and an int age that is at least 18, using Bean Validation annotations.
questions.explanation: Constraints on record components are applied to the accessor and constructor parameter, so validation works when the body is bound with @Valid. @Positive or @Range-style alternatives are equally valid for age.

questions.prompt: Write a Spring GET /users/{id} handler method named find that takes the id as a long path variable, calls service.find(id) returning a UserResponse or null, and answers 404 through ResponseStatusException when the result is null.
questions.explanation: Returning Optional and mapping it with ResponseEntity.of(optional) is another idiom. Throwing a domain NotFoundException that a @RestControllerAdvice maps to 404 keeps controllers clean in larger applications.

questions.prompt: True or false: if a handler declares @PathVariable long id and the client calls /users/abc, Spring answers 400 Bad Request by default.

options.why: Correct: the failed conversion raises MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException, which becomes 400.
Wrong: the failure is neither a missing route (404) nor a server error (500); the client sent a bad value.

questions.explanation: Spring converts path segments to the declared type; a failure is a client mistake and maps to 400, not 404 or 500.

questions.prompt: True or false: by default, Spring MVC answers 422 Unprocessable Entity when a @Valid request body fails Bean Validation.

options.why: Wrong: nothing in Spring maps validation failures to 422 by itself.
Correct: the default is 400 Bad Request; 422 requires your own exception handler.

questions.explanation: Teams that prefer 422 add an @ExceptionHandler for MethodArgumentNotValidException that sets that status. Both choices are defensible if consistent and documented.

questions.prompt: Judge the assertion and the reason.
questions.assertion: Returning a JPA entity directly from a controller can leak fields such as a password hash.
questions.reason: Jackson serialises every readable property of the object unless it is excluded.

whys.a: Correct: without a DTO, @JsonIgnore or a view, all getters end up in the JSON body.
whys.b: Wrong: R is the mechanism behind A.

questions.explanation: Return dedicated response records or DTOs. The same discipline protects against lazy-loading surprises and accidental schema coupling.
